# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-20**
**Member: Avery Alvarez | Member ID: W460125797**
**Reference number: POC-55381BDBC3-44861**
**Plan: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan (Commercial/ACA), Hawaii**
**Governing policy: Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O)** — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of my request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has determined is medically necessary. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial notice states that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I want to walk through the documentation that was submitted so the plan can see what is already in my file, and to explain why I believe the plan's own policy supports my surgery.

The plan's policy states: "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances." It goes on to say: "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:" and lists several categories, including "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

My requested procedure — total ankle replacement — falls under "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle," which the plan's own policy identifies as one of the categories with dedicated InterQual criteria. My file already contains the following documentation relevant to that determination:

- **Symptom duration:** 12 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative care completed:** 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-05-15 to 2026-07-24, 16 visits), documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** 6 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief.
- **Injection trial:** corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29, giving only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-07-12 showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.
- **Functional limitation:** antalgic gait, ambulation limited to two blocks.
- **Exam findings:** positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion.
- **No contraindications:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Given this record, I do not believe the documentation is incomplete with respect to the type of surgery I actually need.

I also want to flag that several portions of the criteria referenced in connection with my denial appear to address a different procedure. The policy states: "Osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant is unproven and not medically necessary for treating cartilage defects of the ankle due to insufficient evidence of efficacy," and separately notes that "however, a considerable number of the allografts failed, requiring repeat allografting, arthrodesis, or arthroplasty (range, 11%-48%)," and that "All studies exhibited a high risk of bias in at least one domain, with 64% demonstrating a high risk across at least four domains." These statements, along with the AOFAS position statement on osteochondral autograft and allograft transplant, concern cartilage-defect treatments (osteochondral allograft/autograft transplant), not total ankle replacement. My surgeon has not requested an osteochondral allograft or autograft procedure. If these criteria were part of the basis for my denial, I believe they were applied to the wrong procedure, and I am asking the plan to clarify and correct this.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The plan's policy states that "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP" and that "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits." Because InterQual is licensed software and not something I can access on my own, I am formally requesting that the plan provide me, in writing and free of charge, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination — specifically the criteria used for "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle." I understand that "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested," and I am not asking for a guarantee of coverage — only for the specific criteria that were used to evaluate my case, so that my surgeon and I can respond to any remaining questions directly.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to reconsider the denial of CPT 27702, to apply the InterQual criteria specific to Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle, and to provide me the full text of those criteria in writing. If any additional records are needed to complete this review, please tell me specifically what is missing so my surgeon's office can provide it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-16. I am submitting it by signing in at member.uhc.com and filing it there [and/or by calling the number on my member ID card], and I am also sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and let me know if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Avery Alvarez
Member ID: W460125797
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date of submission]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Sign in at member.uhc.com and file the appeal there, or call the number on your card. There is no single public appeals fax or PO box — use the address on your denial letter. Online: member.uhc.com By phone: The number on your ID card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Your plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. You have a right to it anyway: federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give you, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for the denial. Ask in writing for 'the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination'.
